headline: LangChain has added a search tool to LangSmith that lets developers find AI agent mistakes by describing them in everyday words.
score_reason: Vendor feature announcement for developers; useful but niche.
importance_line: It helps developers catch agents that say a job is done when it is not, though the search reads only a trimmed 8,000-token view of long sessions and may miss details.
summary: Developer Tech News reports, citing LangChain's announcement, that LangSmith, LangChain's tool for monitoring AI agents, now has AI Search, which lets developers find agent sessions by describing a behaviour such as an agent claiming a task is finished when it is not. LangChain says an AI model reviews each recorded session, but only an 8,000-token portion of long ones, so it may miss details, and the company is working on better ways to pick what to examine.
notes: Company limits (8,000-token budget) are LangChain's statements as relayed by Developer Tech.
